page.layout: One page of text in a single column of verse, with italic emblem titles set between the stanzas. The running head is at the top, the page number at the top left, and a catchword at the lower right. No margin notes are printed; faint marks on the right edge are show-through.

main_text.l: Clarior exurgit virtus, convitia falsa
Crescentem contra quam mala lingua spuit.
Ocyma tunde manu facili, ferientur odore
Ambrosio nares inde fluente tuæ.
Sin eadem rigidè tundas, tum fœtidus inde
(Nautea cui putens cesserit) halat odor.
Sunt quibus ingenium fit pertractabile, loro
Ducere si studeas & retinere leui.
At duris illos si vis cohibere lupatis,
Efficies ut sit durius hisce nihil.
Quale vides corpus, talis cernetur & umbra:
Ex longo longa est, ex breviore brevis.
Principis infequitur mores variabilis aula:
Illaudata malo fit: sed amanda bono.

l.i: Nerion herba, ex Plinio: Sacra piis vitalia,

main_text.l: Nerion est canibus quod & hircis triste venenum,
Humano generi fertur amica salus.
Sic quæ sacra bonis vitalia munera præbent,
Sunt, hominum culpa, tristia facta malis.
Anguibus utilis est pellendis: est bona bello
Fraxinus: in sylvis pulchra: decora domi.
Quàm bene confociat geminas hæc copula dotes,
Si pulchro iungas utile forte pari!

page.notes: The first heading "Nerion herba, ex Plinio" and the line "Sacra piis vitalia" are underlined in the original; the underlining is not transcribed. The left-hand brace beside the Nerion stanza is a typographic device, not text. Some words in the Fraxinus stanza are faint in the scan and "confociat" and "syluis" were read with care. Right-margin marks are show-through and were omitted.
